subject: Freezing rain
hook: FREEZING RAIN IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Freezing rain isn’t frozen rain at all – it’s still liquid when it falls and only turns to ice the moment it contacts a surface
angle_support: Freezing rain is made entirely of liquid droplets... the raindrops become supercooled while passing through a subfreezing layer of air... and then freeze upon impact with any surface they encounter
Freezing rain is rain maintained at temperatures below freezing by the ambient air mass that causes freezing on contact with surfaces
title: Why Freezing Rain Isn't Actually Frozen
description: Discover the science behind freezing rain, a weather phenomenon that is liquid when it falls and only turns to ice upon impact with surfaces. Learn how supercooled droplets create dangerous glaze ice on roads, trees, and aircraft.
narration: FREEZING RAIN IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture ice falling from the sky like hail or sleet. It was closer to liquid water, just hiding a dangerous secret. You assume freezing rain is frozen rain, but the precipitation actually arrives as supercooled droplets that remain liquid until they hit something. As these droplets fall, they pass through a shallow subfreezing layer near the ground. They lack the time to crystallize into ice pellets. Instead, they remain liquid until they touch a surface like a road or a tree branch. Upon contact, they instantly nucleate into a smooth, heavy glaze of ice. This layer conforms to every shape, coating power lines and airfoils in a thick, weight-bearing shell that can snap steel and wood alike. It is not falling ice; it is a liquid trap. The rain is still water when it hits the ground, only becoming ice in that final instant.
